guard_streams.source: What to do if your broadband or landline provider goes out of business

facts.detail: Ofcom published the provider-failure guidance on 13 February 2026.
Where another company takes over, services and contracts should generally continue without interruption.
If the acquiring provider changes contract terms, customers should normally be able to leave without an early termination charge.
If there is no takeover, the service will stop on a notified date and the customer must arrange a replacement provider.
Customers in vulnerable circumstances are advised to tell the provider because additional support may be available.

guard_streams.source: 1.6 million Brits hit switch on their landline or broadband provider

facts.detail: Ofcom published the One Touch Switch milestone update on 12 September 2025.
More than 300 providers were offering One Touch Switch one year after launch.
Ofcom reported that more than 1.6 million customers had switched landline or broadband provider using the process.
The customer contacts only the new provider, which manages the switch and sends switching implications.
Providers must compensate customers for delayed service starts or loss of connection lasting more than one working day.

guard_streams.source: Upgrading landlines to digital technology – what you need to know

facts.detail: Providers should arrange required equipment such as a router or a new broadband installation.
Customers should identify alarms, telecare and other devices that rely on the phone line because they may need replacement or reconfiguration.
After PSTN switch-off, customers keeping a landline will generally need a suitable connection even if they do not use broadband services.
A phone connected through a mains-powered broadband router will not work during a power cut without resilience equipment.
Providers must provide a way for landline-dependent customers to contact emergency services during a power cut.

guard_streams.source: Moving landline phones to digital technology: what you need to know

facts.detail: Digital phones require battery back-up to work during a power cut.
A resilience solution should be provided free to customers who depend on their landline.
The provider should arrange equipment needed to keep the customer's main telephone connected.
The PSTN closure is an industry decision rather than a decision by Ofcom or the UK Government.
Ofcom wrote to industry in January 2026 setting expectations for safe customer migration.
